text:
maria: quick spike notes — I'm worried about flappy private endpoints when upstreams are overloaded. Proposal: add circuit-breaker at control-plane proxy that trips per-customer when 5xx rate > 30% over 1m, fallback to regional peering/relay.
aj: +1, what about DNS affinity? If we rely on resolved private endpoint IPs, client caching means cached bad IPs persist.
karthik: DNS TTLs are the lever. We could short-circuit by returning an alternative set of A records that point to relay... but that changes srcIP semantics.
maria: Exactly — we need to preserve source IP for rate-limiting and billing on some tenants. If we route via relay, srcIP changes and billing logic breaks.
frank: Can we use a nat-preserving relay? e.g., 1:1 NAT from tenant IP->relay so backend sees original IP in header? Risky.
maria: We considered X-Forwarded-For but customers rely on true src, e.g., firewall allowlists.
aj: Idea: two-tier fallback. First, control plane returns a short TTL and removes the unhealthy IP from DNS set. Second, if not recover within circuit window, fallback to peering (preserve src) or dedicated tunnel. Relay only as last resort.
elaine: ops concerns — if we flip DNS aggressively we'll cause churn for mobile clients behind corporate caches. Runbook should include a gradual TTL creep and canary.
frank: +1 on canary. Implementation sketch:
```
cb_threshold = 0.30
cb_window = 60s
dns_ttl_short = 30
canary_pct = 5
```
maria: rollout plan: 1) feature flag per-customer, 2) start canary 5% on staging, 3) monitor 5xx, latency, srcIP preservation, 4) ops playbook to revert DNS changes.
aj: monitoring: need token-level tracing to see billing delta. Also ensure console shows per-route 'circuit state' and reason.
karthik: API surface: add 'circuit_state' to /routes/:id and events to webhook: CIRCUIT_OPEN, CIRCUIT_HALF_OPEN, CIRCUIT_CLOSED. Keep semantics light.
elaine: runbook bullets: how to detect false-positives, how to manually open/close CB, how to flush DNS in global caches, how to remediate peering fallback failures.
ops-bot: deploy-check: CI green -> canary rollout started for tenant: redwood-fixtures-1 -> 5% traffic -> scheduled rollback in 2h if 5xx > 10%.
frank: one more gap: certificate handling for relay vs peering. If we change destination we must ensure SNI and cert chain match, else TLS breaks.
maria: right — need cert routing table that maps hostname->cert on relay and peering. Add cert mustache in operator docs.
karthik: thought: alternative is to preserve endpoint IP but mark it unhealthy and return a different backend port on same IP that proxies preserving src. more invasive.
aj: Let's document tradeoffs clearly in RFC follow-up: preserve-src vs aggressive-relay. I'll draft a short decision doc and link here.
maria: thanks. Action items: @aj draft RFC follow-up, @karthik add API events PR, @elaine write ops runbook stub, @frank spike cert routing. I'll follow-up with timeline tomorrow.
aj: will do. :thumbsup:
